## The bitwise gates {#sec-ch16-gates}

### Summary

A bitwise gate asks whether two builds of snapy compute the same bits. It runs a fixed set of decks with each
build on the same machine and the same device, writes the state after a fixed number of steps, and compares the
files byte for byte. Two gates of this kind are in use: the face-deck harness, built with 16 implicit decks, and
the dump set, which runs 20 one-block cases across the reconstructions, Riemann solvers and equations of state.
A change that should not alter results (a refactor, a move of code to another file, a new storage layout) passes
only if every file is identical; a change that should alter results is expected to fail them, and the failure
names the cases it touched. The gates exist because a tolerance-based test cannot tell a harmless refactor from
a small new error, and a byte comparison can.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Decide whether two builds give identical state, byte for byte, on a fixed set of decks.

**Data.** Reads nothing from a run directory; writes, per build, the harness's `<deck>.pt` and `manifest.json`,
or the dump set's `<case>.hydro_u.bin`, `<case>.scalar_s.bin`, `<case>.json` and `status.json`.

**Placement.** Outside the solver and outside ctest: two Python scripts run against each build's installed
package, then a compare step.

**Activation.** `h348.py --device <dev> --out <dir>` and `dumpset349.py --device <dev> --dtype <dtype> --out
<dir>`, then `h348.py --compare <a> <b>` and `compare.py <a> <b>`. Default: not run.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exit 0 only when every case ran in both runs and every file is byte-identical. Holds
only between runs on one machine and one device: a CPU run is compared with a CPU run, a CUDA run with a CUDA run.

**Evidence.** No ctest at the pin; the gate is its own evidence, run with a control (@tbl-ch16-gates-tests).
:::

Local symbols of this section: $u_{\mathrm{A}}(d)$ and $u_{\mathrm{B}}(d)$ the arrays that builds A and B write for deck $d$;
$n_{\mathrm{step}}$ the number of steps a deck takes.

### Derivation

None: a gate is a method, not a scheme. Its rule is one line. For every deck $d$ of the set, with $u_{\mathrm{A}}(d)$
and $u_{\mathrm{B}}(d)$ the arrays the two builds write after $n_{\mathrm{step}}$ steps,

$$
\text{pass} \iff \forall d:\ \mathrm{bytes}\big(u_{\mathrm{A}}(d)\big) = \mathrm{bytes}\big(u_{\mathrm{B}}(d)\big)
\ \text{ and both runs of } d \text{ finished.}
$$ {#eq-ch16-gate}

@eq-ch16-gate compares the arrays as raw bytes, ghost cells included, so it sees every bit of every variable,
including a sign of zero and a NaN payload. It holds for a pair of runs on one device: the same build gives
different bits on CPU and on CUDA (the floating-point operations are not issued in the same order), so a
CPU-against-CUDA comparison is information only, never a gate.[^ch16-gates-src]

### Numerical method

**The face-deck harness.** `h348.py` builds 16 decks from one function and runs each for $n_{\mathrm{step}} = 10$ steps at a
fixed step: two implicit matrices, two forms of the gravity work and four geometries
(@tbl-ch16-harness). Every deck uses an ideal gas, the positivity limiter, WENO5[^rg-2616ddfc1c3d] in both directions, the LMARS[^rg-7367fe18c296]
solver, rk3, reflecting $x_1$[^rg-01fadbe6e8ea] walls and float64, and a redo raises. The initial state is an isothermal
hydrostatic column with a small density perturbation; the step is fixed at a vertical acoustic Courant number of
about 20, so the implicit solve is exercised. After each step the harness saves `hydro_u`, every variable with its
ghost cells, and `--compare` compares the two `[10, nvar, nc3, nc2, nc1]` arrays of each deck byte for byte; it
also prints, for information, the largest relative difference of the energy row per step.

| axis | values |
|---|---|
| implicit matrix | `full` (`implicit-scheme: 9`), `partial` (`implicit-scheme: 1`) |
| gravity work | `face` (`gravity-work-fixer: false`); `cell` (removed at the pin: `const-gravity`[^rg-b743ab6e7970] refuses it) |
| geometry | `cartesian`, `stretched` ($x_1$ ratio 1.05), `spherical-polar`, `gnomonic-equiangle` |

: The 2 × 2 × 4 decks of the face-deck harness; the deck files are written by `h348.py --write-decks`, whose
`config()` is their one source. {#tbl-ch16-harness}

At the code pin only the 8 `face` decks run. The `cell` form of the gravity work was removed (V3 I-7), and
`const-gravity` refuses it, and a `gravity-work-fixer: true` too, when the deck is read
({{< code src/forcing/const_gravity.cpp >}}); `h348.py` does not catch that error, so a run of the tool as
committed stops at the first `cell` deck and writes no manifest. A gate at the pin needs the `cell` decks removed
from `config()` first.

**The dump set.** `dumpset349.py` runs 20 one-block cases for 20 rk3 steps each at a fixed step that the deck
alone decides, one child process per case, and writes the final `hydro_u` (and `scalar_s` where the case has a
scalar) as raw C-order bytes, ghost cells included: 23 files per run. The cases cover what a step can route
through (@tbl-ch16-dumpset). `compare.py` exits 0 only if both runs have every case at exit code 0 in their
`status.json` and every file is byte-identical; otherwise it lists the cases that differ, failed or are missing,
with the first differing element of each.

| group | cases | what varies |
|---|---|---|
| 2-D box, gravity | 8 | the reconstruction (WENO5 and WENO3[^rg-1d6fbd595d86], each with and without scaling; the scaled shock form; CP5, CP3, PLM[^rg-519f17b4266b]) against the LMARS, HLLC[^rg-2e823fe9fba3] and Roe solvers |
| 3-D box, gravity | 1 | scaled WENO5 with HLLC |
| gnomonic face block, gravity | 3 | scaled WENO5 with LMARS, HLLC and Roe |
| 2048-cell $x_1$ column, no gravity | 3 | the tiled CUDA reconstruction path, with three reconstructions |
| moist box | 4 | ideal-moist with the EOS[^rg-17196f1aab8c] limiter on or off, cloud sedimentation, a passive scalar and a scalar with a zero hole |
| shallow water, periodic | 1 | WENO5 with the shallow-water Roe solver |

: The 20 cases of the dump set, grouped; the case table of `dumpset349/README.md` names each one with its grid,
solver and step. {#tbl-ch16-dumpset}

**The pairing rule.** A gate run pairs the base build and the candidate build on one machine, with identical
build flags, on one device; `gates.sh` runs the harness and the dump set in float64 and the dump set again in
float32, on CPU and on CUDA, and also runs the base twice and compares it with itself. That control matters: a
gate is only meaningful on a device that gives the base the same bits twice.

### Code

**How to use it.** From outside the source tree (so that `import snapy` loads the installed build), with each
build's package first on `PYTHONPATH`:

```sh
python h348.py --device cpu --out runs/base_cpu          # base build
python h348.py --device cpu --out runs/head_cpu          # candidate build
python h348.py --compare runs/base_cpu runs/head_cpu     # exit 0: every deck identical
python dumpset349.py --device cuda --dtype float64 --out runs/base_cuda
python dumpset349.py --device cuda --dtype float64 --out runs/head_cuda
python compare.py runs/base_cuda runs/head_cuda          # exit 0: every case identical
```

**What is refused, and why.** Nothing in `src/` refuses a gate run. The gate fails, by design, when a case does
not finish in one of the runs (a missing file is not equal to a present one), and the harness's decks raise on a
redo, so a step that would have been redone ends the deck instead of hiding in the comparison.

The gates read no symbol of the snapy tree; their code is the four files named in the PROVENANCE block, on the
closing-plan branch. The default build's one ctest that compares a full run with a reference, `test_straka`
(with `FULL_TESTS`, `test_shallow_xy` and `test_shallow_splash` as well; {{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}), is
not a bitwise gate: `test_straka.py` ({{< code tests/test_straka.py >}}) passes when the $L_2$ norm of the potential
temperature difference to the reference run is below 50.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| none at the pin | the gates are tools on the closing-plan branch, not ctest entries | exact (byte for byte) | @eq-ch16-gate |
| base against base, per device | a device gives the base build the same bits twice, so a base-against-candidate difference is the candidate's | exact | the control runs of `gates.sh` |

: Tests of the bitwise gates. {#tbl-ch16-gates-tests}

This chapter quotes no gate result. A gate result belongs to a pair of commits, and the record of each pair is
the review that ran it.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- A gate compares two builds on one device; it says nothing about agreement across devices (@sec-ch16-devices).
- The decks are fixed: a code path that none of the harness decks or 20 cases reaches is not gated. The harness has
  no scalar, no moisture and one Riemann solver; the dump set has no implicit solve.
- Both tools are rebuilt from the case descriptions of the original gates, whose scripts were never committed;
  the deck sizes, initial states and steps are the rebuild's choices.[^ch16-gates-src]
- The stored checksums of the reference runs match only on hardware that gives the reference build the same
  bits; the gate is always a fresh pair of runs, not a comparison with those files.
:::
